# Fifty Pages of Shades — Nick Brand (full reference)

Fifty Pages of Shades is the fine-art photography brand of Nick Brand, a Sydney photographer with more than twenty years' experience. Site: https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/

## What it is
- Contemporary black-and-white abstract photographic art exploring form, texture, light and shadow. Familiar shapes become abstract compositions in which the original subject is secondary to the image.
- The images are entirely non-explicit and often surprisingly difficult to interpret. They sit between abstract photography and contemporary fine art.
- One collection of 17 works, titled "The Art of the Unseen Form": https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/collections/
- Each work is a strictly limited edition of 15, numbered, printed in black and white on canvas, gallery-framed and wired ready to hang. Once an edition sells out it closes permanently and is never reprinted.
- Each work ships with a signed Certificate of Authenticity and a provenance record.
- Custom sizes are available. Frame choices: no frame (gallery wrap), black floating frame, natural oak floating frame, white floating frame. The canvas works have no glass front, so there is no glare and no glass to break.
- Prices start from AUD $1,700 and are set by size and frame; they are shown on each work page. Delivery is Australia-wide and worldwide on request.

## Where to see it in person
- Fifty Pages of Shades is showing at NITA Gallery, 68 Campbell Street, Surry Hills NSW 2010, Sydney.
- NITA Gallery hours: Tuesday and Wednesday 10am-6pm; Thursday 10am-8pm; Friday 10am-6pm; Saturday 10am-3pm; closed Sunday and Monday; open by appointment any day.
- Parking nearby is difficult; Central and Museum stations are close and there is a car park across the road.
- Private viewings for collectors, interior designers, corporate and healthcare buyers: phone Nick on 0403 835 467 or email studio@fiftypagesofshades.com.
- Details: https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/about/exhibitions/ — NITA Gallery: https://www.nitagallery.com.au

## Who it is for
### Collectors
- Limited editions of 15 with certificate and provenance. Guides: how to buy fine art photography (https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/collectors/collector-guide/), and an educational page on photography as an investment (https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/collectors/investment-in-photographic-art/). Art carries no guaranteed financial return; buy first for enjoyment.
- FAQ: https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/resources/faq/ — Glossary: https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/resources/glossary/
### Interior designers and architects
- Trade program: preferred pricing for approved interior designers, architects, developers and art consultants; custom sizes; gallery framing; delivery ready to hang; one point of contact. https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/for-designers/
### Corporate
- Art for offices, receptions, boardrooms, hotels, restaurants and developments; multi-site and cohesive schemes; project-managed. Abstract monochrome, brand-safe. https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/for-designers/corporate-art/
### Hospitals and healthcare
- Calm, abstract black-and-white art for hospitals, day surgeries, clinics, wellness centres and aged care. Canvas with no glass front, custom sizes, delivered across Australia. Facility requirements (cleaning, fixings) are confirmed in writing per project. https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/healthcare-art/
### Commissions and large scale
- A limited number of bespoke commissions each year: https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/commissions/
- Oversized canvas works for feature walls, lobbies and voids: https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/large-scale-art/

## Guides (journal)
- What is abstract photographic art: https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/journal/what-is-abstract-photographic-art/
- How much does fine art photography cost in Australia: https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/journal/how-much-does-fine-art-photography-cost-australia/
- How to choose the right size art for any wall: https://www.fiftypagesofshades.com/journal/how-to-choose-the-right-size-art-for-any-wall/
  (Rule of thumb: a feature work fills about two-thirds of the wall or furniture below it, hung with its centre about 145-150 cm from the floor.)
